deck.title: Secrets Manager & Parameter Store
deck.analogy: Parameter Store is a free key hook board in a locked closet; Secrets Manager is a hotel keycard system that automatically reissues cards on a schedule.

subtopics.title: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point
Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical
The runtime pattern (the "fix the hardcoded password" answer)

cards.front: What do Secrets Manager and Parameter Store have in common, and what is THE differentiator?

back.answer: Both are managed stores encrypted with KMS and fetched at runtime via API; the differentiator is automatic rotation, Secrets Manager only.
back.explanation: Both hold config values and secrets. Only Secrets Manager rotates them automatically.
back.mnemonic: Parameter Store = free key hook board; Secrets Manager = hotel keycards that reissue themselves.

cards.front: How does Secrets Manager natively rotate credentials, and for which services?

back.answer: RDS, Redshift and DocumentDB credentials are rotated via a built-in Lambda it manages; other secrets need a custom rotation Lambda.
back.explanation: Native rotation needs zero custom code.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: What does Secrets Manager cost?

back.answer: $0.40 per secret per month, plus a small per-10k-API-calls fee.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: What is the maximum secret size in Secrets Manager?

back.answer: 64KB.
back.explanation: Parameter Store caps at 4KB standard and 8KB advanced.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: How do you share a Secrets Manager secret with another AWS account?

back.answer: Use a resource policy on the secret (cross-account sharing).
back.explanation: Standard Parameter Store does not support cross-account sharing.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: How are Secrets Manager secrets encrypted and audited?

back.answer: Encrypted with KMS; every access is logged in CloudTrail.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: Why does Secrets Manager rotation cause no application downtime?

back.answer: The app fetches the current secret value at connect time, so it never notices the change.

cards.sourceHeading: Secrets Manager — rotation is the whole point

cards.front: What are the Parameter Store standard tier limits and cost?

back.answer: Free; up to 4KB per parameter and 10,000 parameters.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: How do hierarchical paths help in Parameter Store?

back.answer: Paths like /prod/db/password let one GetParametersByPath call fetch a branch and let IAM be scoped per path.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: Can Parameter Store store encrypted secrets?

back.answer: Yes — the SecureString type is KMS-encrypted.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: What does the Parameter Store Advanced tier add?

back.answer: 8KB size, parameter policies (e.g. expiration notification), higher throughput, for a small fee.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: Does Parameter Store support native automatic rotation?

back.answer: No — that is the dividing line versus Secrets Manager.
back.explanation: If a question requires automatic rotation, Parameter Store is wrong.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: Which service fits app config, feature flags, license keys, AMI IDs or the cheapest option?

back.answer: Parameter Store.

cards.sourceHeading: Parameter Store (SSM Parameter Store) — free and hierarchical

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: automatic rotation?

back.answer: Secrets Manager: yes, native for RDS/Redshift/DocumentDB. Parameter Store: no.

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: cost?

back.answer: Secrets Manager $0.40/secret/month; Parameter Store free (standard tier).

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: max size?

back.answer: Secrets Manager 64KB; Parameter Store 4KB (8KB advanced).

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: hierarchy?

back.answer: Secrets Manager uses flat names; Parameter Store uses paths like /prod/db/...

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: cross-account sharing?

back.answer: Secrets Manager: yes. Parameter Store: no (standard).

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: KMS encryption?

back.answer: Secrets Manager always encrypts; Parameter Store only for the SecureString type.

cards.front: Secrets Manager vs Parameter Store: what is each built for?

back.answer: Secrets Manager: secrets that must rotate. Parameter Store: config plus secrets that don't rotate.

cards.front: What is the decision flow between Secrets Manager and Parameter Store?

back.answer: Needs automatic rotation → Secrets Manager; otherwise cheapest/config/hierarchy → Parameter Store.
back.code:
"rotate automatically"? yes -> Secrets Manager
no -> "cheapest / config / hierarchy"? -> Parameter Store

cards.front: What is the exam-blessed runtime pattern for app secrets with Secrets Manager or Parameter Store?

back.answer: Attach an IAM role to the app; it calls GetSecretValue/GetParameter at runtime and KMS decrypts transparently.
back.explanation: No credentials in code or env files. Both services integrate with Lambda and ECS environment injection.
back.code: App (IAM role) -> GetSecretValue / GetParameter -> KMS decrypts -> connect to DB

cards.sourceHeading: The runtime pattern (the "fix the hardcoded password" answer)

cards.front: Secrets Manager/Parameter Store question: which credential placements are wrong answers?

back.answer: Credentials in code, an AMI, a repo config file, or a plain environment variable are all wrong.
back.explanation: Fix: fetch at runtime via IAM role; if rotation is mentioned, Secrets Manager, so no downtime.

cards.sourceHeading: The runtime pattern (the "fix the hardcoded password" answer)

cards.front: Automatically rotate the RDS database password every 30 days. Which service?

back.answer: Secrets Manager (native RDS rotation via built-in Lambda).

choices.why: Native RDS rotation via built-in Lambda.

cards.front: Store application configuration values at the lowest possible cost. Which service?

back.answer: Parameter Store standard tier (free).

cards.front: Organize config per environment (/prod/db/url, /dev/db/url) with IAM scoped per environment. Which?

back.answer: Parameter Store hierarchical paths.

cards.front: Share a database secret with an application in another AWS account. Which?

back.answer: Secrets Manager cross-account resource policy.

cards.front: Developers hardcoded the DB password in code. What is the fix?

back.answer: Secrets Manager + IAM role; app fetches at runtime.

choices.text: Move it to a plain environment variable
Put it in a repo config file
Secrets Manager with IAM role runtime fetch

cards.front: Store an encrypted license key for free. Which?

back.answer: Parameter Store SecureString (KMS-encrypted, still free).

cards.front: Rotate credentials without application downtime. Which service?

back.answer: Secrets Manager — app fetches the current secret at connection time.

choices.why: Fetches current value at connect time.

cards.front: A secret is 20KB of JSON credentials. Which service?

back.answer: Secrets Manager (64KB limit; Parameter Store caps at 4/8KB).

cards.front: Audit who accessed the database secret. Which?

back.answer: Either service plus CloudTrail (all API access is logged).

choices.text: Only Secrets Manager, with no logging
